by Deimy_in_Bloom

Summary

thanks to a mishap with a suspect artifact, phainon ends up switching places with his past self.

suddenly, he’s back in a time where he and mydei barely knew each other, and not even an hour later he gets punched by his husband’s younger self.

meanwhile, a younger phainon gets thrown into the future, head spinning as he takes in the fact that the older mydei in front of him was… his husband. what.

——

or: time travel shenanigans with phainon. both mydeis are NOT happy with it. only at first though.

Notes

hii hi, it’s me again. if you follow me on twt, then this premise should be familiar. it’s based on a thread i made months ago, but i ended up tweaking it as i truly fleshed the fic out.

this should have two parts: (1) Side A in older Phainon’s pov and (2) Side B in younger Phainon’s pov.

it’s been a while since i wrote a canon-adjacent fic. with that, here’s a few notes about this AU:
1) the eternal recurrences don’t occur here, but phainon’s khaslana form does exist. there is no flame reaver because there is no loop.
2) phainon gained his khaslana form during his ascension in kephale’s coreflame trial.
3) phainon still ends up striking mydei at his weakspot and killing him. the reason will be elaborated in the fic.

lastly, i don’t think this is much of a spoiler, but future phainon WILL be sleeping with past mydei and vice versa, so if you don’t agree with this idea, please exit the fic, thank you!

that’s all, sorry for the yap & i hope you enjoy!

Phainon tips his head back, laying a wet towel over his eyes as he sighs in irritation. The Heroes' Bath was supposed to be a place of relaxation, but every bone in his body feels far from relaxed.

He's in a terribly foul mood, completely over the extermination mission he'd just returned from. He's almost glad that none of his fellow heirs are here to join him. Almost. Because that meant Mydei wasn't here either.

They had agreed to meet at Okhema's gates the moment he returned, but just as he neared the city, Phainon had received a text from his husband, apologizing that he would be unable to make it.

An urgent problem emerged in the Kremnoan detachment, large enough that they'd needed to get their crown prince involved despite being a usually independent group. Phainon completely understands; after all, duty always came first.

That didn't mean his mood hadn't plummeted at the thought of spending the day without his husband by his side.

Now, he sits in the bath all alone, irritated and lonely, and not even putting on a pomegranate scent could alleviate his mood at all. If anything, it only makes him miss his husband more.

Sighing, he gives up, removing the towel over his eyes and callously throwing it to the side. He knows now that the baths would do nothing for him, so he might as well call it a night and catch up on some sleep.

He changes into a clean set of his usual garments Mydei left for him ahead of time, a sweet gesture to show that he was truly sorry he'd be unable to join Phainon in their favorite bonding activity (alright, perhaps it was just Phainon's favorite). He'd even left a slice of honeycake beside them with a note that said: Just in case Little Ica got to it first, I left you a slice of cake. If they managed to, don't worry, there's more at home. I love you <3.

Cute. So cute. His husband was so cute. The note makes Phainon groan fondly into his hands, and he's had to take deep breaths as he crouches in front of the little stool Mydei had prepared for him. Phainon reminds himself to give him a sweet peck the moment he sees him.

He ate the slice earlier, and it had admittedly lifted his spirits, but only just, because sitting in the bath alone, munching on Mydei's homemade honeycake, only reminded him of his husbandless state. And his mood worsens once more.

Titans, I must be losing it, Phainon thinks uncharitably as he exits the bath. It's quite late by now, only a few people milling about here and there, so he takes the scenic route to calm his temper.

If he arrives home in this state and Mydei's already waiting for him, he'd see right through Phainon's attempts at levity and start fretting in that quiet way of his. Worse, he might even feel guilty for unintentionally blowing Phainon off, and he'd apologize with that soft moue of his lips that only appears when he's feeling guilty. An adorable sight, but not one Phainon wants to see when he knows his husband is feeling terrible.

Phainon would never be the cause of Mydei's distress if he could help it. His husband has gone through enough.

He's only halfway home when he spots the group of drunkards that usually frequent Okhema's biggest pub, ambling the streets with drunken clumsiness and slurred words. Phainon winces internally. They can't spot him now, or they'll drag him into a barely intelligible conversation, and Phainon has no patience for it at the moment, Deliverer or no.

He swiftly ducks into an obscured alleyway, eyes slowly adjusting to the dim light as he navigates through the dark when he accidentally crashes into something coming at him at high speed.

“Nya-ow!”

—or someone.

“Lady Cifera?” He calls, recognizing her voice. He's only spoken to her a handful of times, more outside Okhema than inside, usually coming up to him in the most random places, selling him suspect wares she claimed she had gathered throughout her travels. It's certainly a surprise to see her here in a random alley in the middle of the night… cursing him out in Dolosian.

His eyes finally adjust to the dark, and he can make out the way her body stiffens as she recognizes his voice in turn. She clears her throat, and all the ire in her voice is gone as she goes, “Heyyy, Deliverer Boy! Fancy seeing you here!”

He squints at her incredulously. “Well, I live here.”

“Ha! So you do!” She clicks her fingers, trying to sound jovial, but she's so obviously distracted, looking at the ground by their feet. "Didn't expect our golden boy to be lurking in alleyways, though. Did you and Little Prince fight?"

"What are you doing?" Phainon asks, ignoring her blatant attempt at flustering him. He tilts his head, trying to make sense of her stranger-than-usual behavior. “Did you drop something?”

“I'm a nimble cat, Deliverer Boy, there’s no way I’d drop anything,” Cipher answers, shuffling around.

Phainon takes a step back when a tail whacks him on the face, and nearly tips over when he steps on something hard and spherical. “I think I stepped on something.”

He bends down to pick it up, the cold metal brushing his hand when Cipher hisses and cries out.

“Wait, don’t pick it up—”

Phainon jolts when the cold metal turns searing hot in his hand, and he goes to throw it, but it sticks to his hand like a limpet, and something in the hollow of the sphere rattles as he swings his arm around.

“Wait, wait, wait, stop! Stop swinging it around—! Uh-oh.”

“What is happening,” Phainon demands through gritted teeth, his patience thinning. The pain in his palm is nearly unbearable, but he can’t pull it away without risking tearing the skin.

He wishes he could be home with Mydei right now instead of being dragged into one of Lady Cipher’s suspect shenanigans.

Divine can sense the divine; unlike Mydei, who’s yet to inherit the Strife coreflame, Aglaea and Castorice had known that Phainon was no longer as mortal as he was the last time they saw him the moment Mydei dragged him into the Hero’s bath, gauntleted hand clasped tightly around his wrist.

Castorice only tightens her grip on her scythe as she looks away, while Tribbie hides behind a certain prince’s sandaled leg.

 

Phainon brushes the rejection off. It’s only natural that they would be all unsettled by his presence. The only one who seems angry is Mydei, who’s still huffing like a bull at Phainon’s early transgression. He had tried to apologize on the way to the palace, but it seems like Mydei really despised the comment about his nipples.

 

Aglaea looks unhappy. Ah, it seems she had sensed his amusement because she began the interrogation—er, trial—without warning. Her threads and eyes glow in tandem as she speaks, voice crisp as it echoes in the large space.

 

“The trial shall begin. If you are who you claim you are, then I assume you already know how this works.”

 

Phainon nods amicably. “Four questions, three steps. The threads would vibrate for every dishonest answer, and the executioner would step forward for every instance, ensuring my imminent death.”

 

“If Castorice does not end up standing behind you after all four questions are asked, you pass the trial,” Aglaea continues coldly. She looks to Castorice, who nods as she twirls her large scythe around.

 

“Lord… Phainon,” Castorice hesitates, eyes flicking between him and Aglaea, “You should feel no pain in death’s embrace. It will only feel like falling into a deep sleep.”

 

“That’s alright, Castorice,” Phainon says warmly. He’d forgotten for a moment, but this Castorice has yet to know the warmth of the living’s embrace. One day, though, she will learn to control the curse that has controlled her her entire life, and Phainon will be happy for her. “Death has always been an old friend.”

 

Castorice’s eyes widen, her grip on her scythe trembling at the pointed note in Phainon’s voice. Behind her, Mydei blinks, looking conflicted when the implications sink in. Phainon wonders what’s running through his head.

Phainon sighs, standing from his crouch as he reaches out to shut the hose off. No use risking more drowned crops. “I just… I just think that I should’ve seen it coming, yet I didn’t,” he runs a hand through his hair. “Was I being too optimistic, perhaps?”

Mydei steps closer, wiping his dirt-stained hands into his apron. His gaze is piercing as he studies Phainon’s dejected expression. “Of course not. None of us had expected it.”

Tribbie summoned a tome once everyone had settled around the couch. It was almost as large as her, yet she flipped it open with ease, skimming until she reached a certain page. She placed it on the coffee table for everyone to see, and Cyrene picked it up, scanning the page. “We found a spell that could bring Little Snowy back to his timeline.”

Mydei sipped at his cup of tea, observing Cyrene’s carefully blank expression before he spoke, “Is there a problem with the spell?”

Tribbie shook her head. “Not exactly. This tomb was located deep in the lower levels of Marmoreal Palace’s vault, which means it’s been there since Imperator Cerydra’s reign. And she doesn’t keep useless things inside the vault.”

Everyone nodded. Though he didn’t know Imperator Cerydra personally, he knew of her and Hysilens thanks to anecdotes from Aglaea and the Tribios triplets. Aglaea spoke of them with detached admiration, but there was also a wistfulness in her gaze that belied personal attachment. He wondered often what their relationship beyond the crown was.

“Its conditions are simple,” Tribbie went on, snapping Phainon out of his thoughts. “The person displaced must be switched for at least five days, to ensure the stability of the soul. The spell also requires a priestess familiar with time to act as the focal, to ensure a safe transition in time.”

“So that’s why you said you needed me,” Cyrene said, finally looking up. “It’s no problem. The spell is doable and should be safe enough,” she winked at Phainon, who was wringing his hands nervously. “Leave it to Big Sis Cyrene~”

Phainon stared at her. “Could it be… are you Oronyx’s successor?”

Cyrene shrugged playfully. “Good guess, but nope! I’m simply familiar with time magic.”

Phainon scowled at her. He was so sure he got it right.

“There’s one more thing,” Tribbie said. They all turned to her, but she hesitated, tapping a finger on her chin. “There’s a passage on the next page, detailing the artifact’s history. It mentions that… the person’s past self would forget their displacement. As a safeguard for the future.”

Phainon froze, his heart dropping to his feet. Mydei seemed taken aback as well, hand paused as it hovers over the cup he’d placed down earlier. Only Cyrene seems unsurprised, but she looked visibly resigned.

“I had suspected something along those lines,” she murmured, shooting Phainon a sympathetic look. Phainon swallowed as he felt his heart ache. He avoided her gaze, his eyes landing on the tome instead. “A time displacement was always something to be wary of. If the person makes different choices after seeing a glimpse of the future, the consequences may be disastrous, and the future they’ve seen may never exist.”

“The butterfly effect,” Mydei supplied. Phainon peeked at his face, but Mydei’s face remained stony… unreadable. So different from the warm slimes he’d shown Phainon in the past few days. It was almost like seeing the Mydei from his own timeline. “I see.”

Phainon exhaled. “So… once I go back… I’ll forget everything I’ve learned here?” He’d forget that he’d succeeded in his duties? Forget that he was Mydei’s husband? Forget what it felt like to have him in his arms?

Tribbie stared at him with watery eyes, her frown dangerously close to pitying. “I’m sorry, Little Snowy. It’s the spell’s effects.”

Phainon nodded, straightening as he looked away. He didn’t like being pitied, and the silence that engulfed the room only made him feel colder and alone. “It’s okay, Teacher. I understand.”

Cyrene cleared her throat. “The tome said that it is best to do the spell during dusk, during the transition from Kephale’s reign to Oronyx’s. It’s still the Entry Hour… plenty of time for you and Mydei to spend time together before goodbye, Phainon.”

Phainon bit his tongue. It wasn’t enough, he thought. But now was not the time to lash out. He didn’t belong here, after all. He needed to go back. Face blank, he nodded once more.

“You said at least five days. Can’t we do the spell tomorrow?” Mydei asked, stunning Phainon into looking up. He stared at Mydei’s profile, and suddenly, he didn't look so unreadable. He’s visibly upset, staring at Cyrene and Tribbie with a frown.

Cyrene shook her head, apologetic. She flipped the book, her manicured finger pointing at a rune inscribed on the page. “See that rune? It’s one for crossroads. Today is the sixth day since Phainon arrived here. The day between the fifth—the date mentioned in the spell, and the seventh—which is the end of the week. This is our most auspicious opportunity. The magic would have a higher chance of switching his and his future self’s places safely.”

Phainon deflated. Cyrene was the biggest romantic he knew. If they had more than a day, then she’d give them that. She always hated sad partings, though she insisted they made reunions more bittersweet; like the peaches she preferred—sweet but a bit tart from being picked too early. She was sometimes strange like that.

Mydei seemed to know this as well. It was a bit surreal sometimes, seeing how well they got along. His future self was truly fortunate to have them both in his life. “…I see. I have one more question.”

Cyrene nods. “Go ahead, Dei.”

His eyes narrowed as he pointed at a paragraph. “It says here that the switch back will bring both selves to the last place they’ve been. Does this mean that Phainon,” Mydei reached out to squeeze his hand, “would be transported to wherever our time’s Phainon had been back in the past?”

Tribbie leaned forward, then turned the book back to her to scrutinize the paragraph. Eventually, she nodded. “Yes, that’s right. It should be safe enough. And since your past self is in Okhema, we can be certain of his location.”

Mydei sighed while Cyrene giggled. Phainon chuckled, scratching at his neck sheepishly. That was probably the case, try as he might to deny it. His lecherous future self must’ve taken the chance to put his hands all over Mydei, doing as he pleased!

Though Mydei probably wouldn’t let him… right? After all, they barely knew each other, and Phainon had yet to court him and make Mydei fall in love with him. So nothing probably happened, and his future self must be suffering from blue balls. Hah, served him right.

Mydei seemed oblivious to his venemous thoughts, though Cyrene shot him a smug, mocking look. He resisted the urge to stick his tongue out at her, telling himself that they weren’t kids anymore.

“So there is no risk that Phainon would return to the Aedes Elysiae of the past? This place… would be swarming with corrupted titankin then.”

Cyrene smiled. “No, he won’t. I’ll make sure of it.”

Mydei visibly relaxed, assured by her confidence. “That’s all I want to know.”

“Great!” Cyrene beamed, jumping to her feet. “Then Tribbie and I will leave you two be. Remember to meet us at my place at dusk, alright? I’ll have everything ready then.”

Mydei had invited Phainon to join him in watering their garden once Cyrene and Tribbie left, and he jumped at the chance to occupy his mind. They wash up and change into simpler chitons in their own rooms before Mydei leads him to the garden, handing him a freshly steamed bun from who knows where.

Still, he munches on it as Mydei directs him to take their tools out of the tiny shed by the edge of their property, appreciating the tart taste of the pomegranate filling. Phainon soon finds himself enjoying the domesticity of caring for their crops together though his mind had clearly wandered eventually.

Phainon sighs. “I just… I don’t want to forget you, Mydei. I planned to cherish my time here once I returned to the past. And it’s like you said… Now that I know what’s at stake, I’d work harder. I’d tell Aglaea and the others, share the wonderful news, so we could all come up with a better plan to make sure this future that I’ve experienced would come true.”

Mydei opens his mouth to speak, but Phainon continues, shutting his eyes as he pathetically lays out his feelings, like a desperate worshipper hoping for salvation.

“But the biggest reason why I don’t want to forget is that I am enamored by this future. I love being your husband, I love seeing my best friend alive and happy, and I love knowing that everyone got to fulfill their wishes. I’m aware that I’m merely a visitor here, and I’m being utterly shameless right now—”

Mydei clamps a hand over his mouth, looking exasperated. “Stop talking.”

Phainon makes an outraged noise behind Mydei’s hand, but makes no move to remove it. The hand is smooth, so unlike his own, which was rough with callouses, and he’s nearly tempted to lick it when he smells Mydei’s strawberry-scented hand cream.

Mydei sighs, glaring grumpily at Phainon as he takes his hand off. Phainon feels like he missed a few steps here. Why is his husband upset? And why is his tiny pout so adorable? Does Mydei know how kissable it looks?

“I know that my husband has a terrible habit of looking down on himself,” Mydei huffs as he takes Phainon’s hands in his. Phainon tries not to notice that Mydei’s were still smaller than his despite him being taller. “It’s something that I’m working on even after all these years, which is why I will tell you this.”

Phainon holds his breath as Mydei looks him in the eye, golden eyes glowing intensely, as if he were commanding an arduous battlefield.

“My Phainon is so kind and empathetic to others, yet he thinks he doesn’t give himself the same grace. He’s incredibly determined to save his world, yet he doesn’t see himself as part of it. He takes his duties seriously, which is why he seems to think that having desires outside of the Deliverer is selfish, so he tears himself apart for it, though it has never been.”

“Mydei…” Phainon’s heart twists in his chest, and he can feel his eyes water. He hasn’t cried since he’d set off from Aedes Elysiae all by himself. But the moment he’d stepped foot into the future, it was as if the tears he’d dammed up had finally overflowed, just waiting to spill out.

“Phainon. Although you are the destined Deliverer, you are human too. Desires and wishes are part and parcel of being one. If you are enamored by this future, that’s to be expected. It is not shameless to want this, especially now that you have been given a chance to experience everything that you’ve ever wanted.

“So it’s alright to be upset too. Let yourself go. Lash out, weep, every emotion you deem ugly, reveal it to me,” Mydei smiles, brilliant and so, so kind. “I am your husband and your kindred spirit. There is nothing that you can do that would send me running.”

Just like that, Mydei completely shatters the walls he’d built for years, the ones he’d created to keep the little kid—the once dreamer who yearned to go on romantic adventures—within the deepest recesses of his mind after everything had fallen apart. He sobs into Mydei’s arms right in the middle of their garden, burying his face in his chest and holding his husband tightly, not wanting to let go.

Mydei clutches him just as tightly, resting his chin on top of Phainon’s head, alternating between pressing kisses and nuzzling his cheek affectionately.

When Cyrene had first laid out her tarot cards on his bed on their very first sleepover, she’d picked out the Deliverer card while reading his fortune and never picked out anything else since then. Their other friends would have different cards detailing their fates picked out depending on the day, but Phainon’s remained the same.

At first, he’d been delighted. He always wanted to be a hero who would save many. Rescue a damsel from a tower guarded by a dragon. Assist in a coup led by a banished prince against a tyrant king. Every romantic adventure that he and Cyrene had obsessed over, he used to daydream about them as he frolicked over golden wheat fields.

But then the Black Tide came, and suddenly nothing seemed to matter anymore. Every day had been agonizing, and he’d wandered aimlessly, contemplating his purpose. Cyrene said he was a Deliverer. But he couldn’t even save his own hometown.

Still, he kept the card close to his heart, wondering if anything would change. Then he’d arrived in Okhema and discovered his prophecy, his duty, his role in their world. Something had woken up in him after that, like a phoenix risen from its own ashes. He worked hard despite the council’s protests, kept his head high, and made friends with the people of Okhema until they slowly learned to accept him.

At first, he did so as a desperate bid to stay, to keep his place next to Aglaea’s side, just so he won’t have to be alone any longer. Over time, he grew to accept the title of Deliverer once more, especially after Aglaea sent him to the Grove to study under Professor Anaxa’s tutelage.

He’d made wonderful friends again. Spent his days messing around with Hyacine and Castorice and it almost felt like he was back in that golden wheat field. Professor Anaxa had been a good teacher to him as well, and his lackadaisical approach to worshipping divinity helped with stabilizing his views of the Titans and the resentment that festered within him.

The elders of Aedes Elysiae had frequently boasted about Oronyx’s favor, evidenced by the eternal dawn that befell their small town. Yet Oronyx hadn’t lifted a finger when the town they protected had been breached, consumed alive by the tide.

That had been his first mistake. There was no use in depending on the gods to save them. If humanity wanted to be saved, then they could only depend on themselves. It’s why Imperator Cerydra had chosen to fight, why Teacher Tribbie had taken those first steps for the Flame Chase, why Aglaea had held on for so long even as the chilling divinity of Romance had swallowed up her emotions.

He’d thought the path was clear, and Phainon had dedicated himself to the Flame Chase. Yet something had stopped him from officially swearing himself to the cause. Aglaea and Tribbie were patient with him, never pressuring, and he’d been pressuring himself more than ever as if to compensate.

But then Mydei arrived, and suddenly he understood. Despite convincing himself he had nothing to live for but the Flame Chase, that his desire to save Amphoreus trumped all, some small part of him—coming from the same little dreamer—had protested. He needed one more push, one more puzzle piece that would convince him to fully give himself to the cause, and that had been Mydei.

He’d seen himself reflected in the prince’s gait, the way he carried duty and responsibility on broad, sturdy shoulders even though he was years younger than Phainon. Those clear eyes that had always looked ahead unafraid had inspired him.

Because that had been the truth of his hesitation. Phainon had been afraid. Terrified that despite the prophecy, he wouldn’t be enough. That in the end, he’d lose the companions he loved dearly and fail to save Amphoreus on top of that. He’d lost his entire world once. He couldn’t bear to lose it again.

Mydei taught him things. Despite their meager conversations, that one spar they had revealed more than what words could. It didn’t matter if he was enough or not. The only thing that did was choosing to fight again and again, even beyond the very end, and refusing to give up.

“I don’t want to forget,” Phainon warbles into Mydei’s chest. “I want to remember. I need to remember this. I want to hold this memory close to my heart as I take the Flame Chase journey.” He wants to be human and not just be the perfect Deliverer.

“Even if your mind does not, your heart will. Trust in it, husband. Every feeling you hold will remain true even as the memory fades. It’s always been your strongest asset, the heart of a hero.”

Phainon pounces, tipping the two of them until they’re rolling in the grass. He slots their lips together desperately, licking into Mydei’s mouth and sobbing when Mydei opens up easily, cupping Phainon’s cheeks tenderly and tilting his head for a better angle.

He holds Phainon through it all. “I love you,” Phainon confesses the moment they part.

Mydei chuckles fondly. “And I love you. Let’s make the most of the time we have left, hm?”

Phainon closes his eyes, feeling at peace. “Okay.”

─── ⋆⋅☼⋅⋆ ───

They spend a quint just lying in the middle of their garden, staring up at the sky until the dampness of the muddy soil becomes too much. Phainon gets up first, turning to Mydei as he pretends his eyes aren’t swollen from crying, cheerfully asking if he’d like to bathe with him.

For some reason, Mydei snorts. “Sure, husband. I’d love to.”

They head to the public bath where they bumped into the Astral Express, and Phainon has to suffer the ribbing from both Stelle and Caelus, and their group nearly gets kicked out when he decides he’s had enough of them teasing him about the love bites and scratches that littered his torso and attempts to drown them by dunking their heads underwater.

They struggle like wriggling fish, both reaching out to March and Dan Heng, but both of them pretend not to notice. They chat with Mydei instead, which Mydei indulges with amusement.

They go their separate ways after the bath. Each member of the Astral Express wraps him in a hug as they say their goodbyes. Dan Heng tells him that they needed to leave for a planet called Penacony. It seemed that the sister of one of their members he hasn’t met was throwing a concert, and they’ve been invited to watch.

“See you tomorrow!” March beams at him as she pulls away from their hug. Then her eyes flash red and her entire demeanor changes as she throws him a smirk. “Everything will work out fine, Deliverer.”

Phainon blinks, bewildered, but March turns around and shoots him a casual wave as she walks away. Mydei makes a small noise of recognition next to him as he waves back, prompting Phainon to do the same.

“That was Evernight,” Mydei explains as they head to Cyrene’s abode. They walk slowly, taking the scenic route while they hold hands. Mydei points to a pair of dromases grazing the wheat in a field next to Castrum Kremnos’ hulking floating mass. “She’s… hm, March’s guardian, I suppose. That’s Kokopo III, our son, and that’s our daughter-in-law.”

“Is she possessing her?” Phainon asks as he eyes Castrum Kremnos. “They’re cute. When did Castrum Kremnos arrive?”

“I don’t know the exact details but… I suppose I can tell you this. She and March are Oronyx’s successors,” When Phainon turns to him in shock, Mydei smirks. “I’m not telling you more. And the castle arrived while we were speaking with Teacher Tribbie and Cyrene.”

“I was so sure that Cyrene would be the one to inherit Their coreflame,” Phainon mumbles just as they reach the entrance of the temple, located next to Cyrene’s living quarters. There’s a guard stationed just outside, and he perks up when he spots them.

“Good day, my lords!” he salutes. He seems to be Kremnoan, judging by the red, lion-shaped badge he wears over his uniform. Though the Kremnoan dynasty had been dissolved, their reverence for Mydei had not. “Lady Tribbie and Priestess Cyrene are already inside waiting.”

Mydei seems surprised to see him. “You’re here. Weren’t you at the Grove?”

He laughs, scratching at his cheek shyly. “I took a brief sabbatical for my thesis, Sir. I decided to come back home for the festival… but then I volunteered as a temple guard since you… Ah,” he glances at Phainon hesitantly, “sent Andreas back to Okhema.”

Phainon stiffens at the name. He deliberately hadn’t asked about Andreas, afraid that his mood would sour and ruin their time left together. So Mydei had sent him packing. Vicious satisfaction crawls up his chest, and this time he doesn’t shy away from the ugly emotion. Mydei told him it was okay, after all.

Mydei nods gratefully, accepting the explanation easily, the mention of Andreas hardly fazing him. “You’re a good man. Your brother would be proud.”

The guard beams at him as he steps aside, and they enter the temple to find Tribbie and Cyrene waiting for them at the altar. Phainon’s heart pounds; if he didn’t know better, he would've thought he and Mydei were here to get married.

But the incomplete magic circle pulsing eerily in the middle of the temple floor says otherwise. Cyrene turns and gives them a cheerful wave, but Phainon merely scowls back at her.

“Oh, dear,” Cyrene says laughingly. “What’s got you sulking, silly little oryx? What did I do this time?”

Phainon’s mouth twitches at the corner but he tamps his smile down. Little Oryx had been her childhood nickname for him ever since he’d been chased by one and cried in her arms like a baby as he begged her to help him.

“So you really aren’t Oronyx’s successor.”

“Are you still on about that?” Cyrene laughs as they approach her, carefully sidestepping the circle. “Ah, let me guess. Did March tell you who she is?”

Mydei shakes his head. “Evernight took over briefly to bid him farewell.”

Cyrene’s smile grows. “Oh, Ever. She’s the same as always. Coming and going when she wants to.”

Tribbie flies towards them, circling over their heads twice nervously. “Little Snowy, we hope you had a great time. Agy sends her best wishes, and told us to tell you to take things one day at a time.”

Phainon smiles. It seems Aglaea would never stop worrying about him, after all. “Thank you, Teacher Tribbie. I had the best time,” he shoots Mydei a brief glance, “indeed. It’s a shame that my mind would forget but… I think my heart is ready. Please tell Aglaea that her words mean a lot to me.”

Tribbie beams. “Oh, Little Snowy. We’ll miss you dearly. The road ahead will be tough, but we know you’ll make it through. Let’s see each other at the end of the west wind, okay?”

Phainon nods, then turns to Cyrene. She reaches out to give him a bear hug. Phainon clutches her back, burying his face into her hair and inhaling the same peach shampoo she used back then.

“See you soon, Phainon. We shall reunite when dawn breaks.”

Phainon steps back and finally turns to Mydei, then yelps when Mydei grabs him by the collar and slots their lips together messily. Phainon groans, leaning closer to return the kiss.

“See you around, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae. Don’t you dare forget about me completely.”

Phainon chuckles. “Forget you? Like I’d ever,” he taps at his chest, right where his heart is. “You’re my husband. You have the best spot in here.”

Mydei smiles, and Phainon trembles when he notices the tears pooling in the corner of his eyes. Oh. Mydei was— “I would divorce you if I were in anything less.”

“Hey!” Phainon protests as he steps in the middle of the magic circle. Cyrene summons her staff, the familiar crescent head shining pink with her magic. Phainon frowns as he suddenly remembers something. “If I won’t remember about this, does this mean that everyone in the past won’t remember my future self’s visit either?”

“That’s right,” Cyrene tells him. “It would be like nothing happened, but of course,” she winks at him, “we all know how our experiences shape us, whether we remember them or not.”

They really are working hard to assure him. Phainon smiles back, appreciating the effort. “Okay,” he exhales. “I’m ready.”

Cyrene raises her staff, and the magic circle glows brighter as it etches itself into completion, filling in the missing runes that would activate the spell. He can hardly see through the bright light surrounding him, but his eyes lock onto Mydei’s anyway.

Tribbie’s “See you tomorrow!” echoes in his ears as he takes in his fill, etching this Mydei’s into memory for the last time. He notes the way Mydei gives him a little wave, his sunset hair swaying in the wind, and the singular tear streak running down his cheek. Phainon follows its path with his eyes, gasping when it drops to the floor and a lily grows in its place.

Before he can move to comfort Mydei, he’s suddenly plunged into a vast and deep sea. It’s empty save for himself, and he’s surrounded by darkness. He tries to move his limbs, to swim upwards, but his limbs remain locked in place.

The deeper he sinks, the more his memories of his time in the future fade. He struggles at first, desperately clinging to them, building haphazard walls despite knowing their futility. Eventually, he lets himself sink deeper as the water fills his nostrils, and he finds himself wondering.

Hm? What was I… fighting so hard against?

He feels at home in the sea, and the deeper he goes, the calmer he gets. He’s about to shut his eyes when he feels a sharp gaze on him, and when he turns his head to the side, he flinches as a shockingly familiar face stares back.

It’s him… an older version of him. He looks pensive as he stares back, though he has no idea why. As he’s pulled down, his older version seems to be pulled in the opposite direction. Eventually, the man speaks.

“Remember to never submit to the destruction,” his voice is surprisingly clear when it should’ve been muffled by the water. “Take your fate into your own hands and wield it. Hold on to that feeling in your heart for it will light the path of the Flame Chase.”

Phainon blinks, feeling sluggish. What was the other him talking about? He needs to wake up… and report to Aglaea. After that he’ll patrol Okhema, making sure to pass by the Kremnoan Settlement to catch a glimpse of the prince.

His older self smiles coldly. “When you are in a pinch, activate Protocol Agape. It will help you as you face THEM, The Supreme Executioner and THEIR followers.”

Phainon closes his eyes, then lets the calm waters lull him to sleep.

─── ⋆⋅☼⋅⋆ ───

When he opens his eyes, three figures stare back. Tribbie and Cyrene stand by the altar of the temple with hopeful eyes, taking him in. To the side stands Mydei, his arms crossed and face unreadable.

He takes one step, then another, then breaks the magic circle keeping him in place with one downward arc of his hand, running to his husband. He wraps his hands around that familiar, tiny waist and spins him around in the air.

“Husband, I’m back! Did you miss me?”

Mydei chuckles, brushing a gentle hand through his locks. “Not at all,” he lies as he leans down to press a kiss to his temple. “Did you have fun playing around with my younger self, Phainon?”

Phainon freezes, settling Mydei back down gently. He clears his throat, scratching at his nape. “Hm, it seems you know me too well.”

“We’ve been married for nearly a decade,” Mydei says, a sly smile on his face. “I would’ve been more surprised if you told me you hadn’t teased me at least once.”

Phainon’s grip on Mydei’s waist tightens as he pulls him closer, leaning down to nuzzle their noses together. “And what about you, hm? Did you like having an eager puppy around?” He asks as he kisses his husband’s bright red ear. “Woof.”

“HKS,” Mydei hisses, but makes no move to shove him away even as Phainon’s lips trail lower, down to the rapid pulse of his neck. “You just got back and you’re already pawing at me?”

“I need to erase his touch,” Phainon mutters. “I’m sure he put his virgin hands all over you, that opportunistic lech. Probably fumbled around, not knowing what to do with them as they touched your most sensitive parts.”

“You’re pathetic,” Mydei says scathingly, though his grip on his hair tightens as he lets out a shaky breath under Phainon’s relentless ministrations. “Are you actually jealous of your younger self?”

“Ehem!” Cyrene clears her throat pointedly. Phainon glances at her, and she glares back playfully with her hands on her hips. “We’re still here, you know! Please keep the PDA to a minimum!”

Mydei makes a small noise of embarrassment as he tries to back away, but Phainon firmly keeps him in place by his grip on his waist. He smiles at Cyrene sweetly. “Hello, Cyrene, Teacher Tribbie. Shall we speak about this incident tomorrow? I’d like to spend time with my husband after a long time away.”

He tugs Mydei in the direction of the giant double doors without waiting for their reply. Mydei hisses as he digs his heels in, berating Phainon. “Husband, don’t be rude—”

“Wait, at least tell us where the artifact that created this mess is!” Cyrene calls after them. “Aglaea would like to have it for safekeeping!”

“It’s in safe hands,” Phainon says, pausing to throw her a secretive smile over his shoulder. “I gave it to the only person who could keep it safe.”

Cyrene blinks, and Tribbie tilts her head, confused. Phainon shoots them a grin, bright and obnoxious. “Just trust me. Now bye!”

“Phainon!” Mydei protests once more as they burst through the doors, startling the guard keeping watch. He sounds more amused this time, though, so Phainon counts it as a win. “What are you in such a rush for?” he asks as he entwines their hands.

“I just—” His eyes meet the guard’s wide ones, causing him to stop in place. “… Augustus? Is that you?”

The guard squeaks, his cheeks flushing as he looks up at Phainon with starry eyes. “Lord Phainon! I’m sorry, I wasn’t aware that you knew me.”

“Of course I do,” Phainon says distantly, marveling at how well Augustus had grown. He almost looked like a clone of Cassius, who he knows is currently stationed at Okhema. “You're Cassius’ younger brother.”

Augustus lights up, eyes glowing brighter at the mention of his brother. “I see! Forgive me, Lord Phainon. I was simply surprised. I’ve been studying at the Grove for the past ten years, and I haven’t been in Okhema since I was six. Though I am honored you recognized me!”

Phainon grins. It seems time hadn’t changed Augustus’ temperament much. He was still as cheerful as he’d been back when he was a little kid. “You’ve been studying well, I see. Please send my regards to Cassius when you see him.”

As they walk away, Mydei leans in to whisper, “You seem to recognize him as more than Cassius’ younger brother.”

Phainon chuckles, kissing the top of his head. His husband was so cute. “Aw don’t be jealous, love. You know you’re the only one for me. Don’t worry, it will all make sense soon.”

Mydei flushes, scowling. “What—I am not jealous. I was simply asking a question.”

“Whatever you say, my love.”

“I am not!”

─── ⋆⋅☼⋅⋆ ───

They find a woman sitting on the front steps of their home, her tail flicking back-and-forth smugly as she smirks at them. “Yo, Ex-Deliverer Boy. Welcome back. Aren’t ya glad our plan worked out?”

Mydei stares at Cipher, head tilted as he tries to make sense of her words. He glances at Phainon curiously when he says, “I finally get why you were so determined to avoid me all these years.”

“What are you two talking about?” Mydei asks as Cipher cackles, her grin mischievous and proud as a cat that caught the canary as she turns to Mydei.

“You see. little lion, your husband over here and past me made a plan twenty years ago,” she grins at Mydei’s stunned face, shrugging her shoulders as she says. “Mhm, you understood right. I meant this Phainon and the me he’d encountered while he was stuck in the past.”

“Lady Cipher,” Phainon greets lightly, “What are you doing here?”

The Trickery demigod finally emerges from her hiding place, a Cheshire-like grin on her face. “I’m here because I heard a certain future Deliverer Boy needed my help. But let’s keep this between us. No need to alert Aglaea, yeah?”

His eyebrows raise, intrigued. “Why not?”

Cipher sighs dramatically. “So skeptical, geez. It's not nice to treat a lady that way, y’know?” When Phainon remains unmoved, she drops all pretense. “Alright, fine. I’d rather not tell Agy because the fewer people that know, the better it would be for all of us.”

She summons a tome in her hands and flicks it at Phainon, who catches it easily with one hand. She clicks her tongue at him, but he ignores it as he skims through it.

“I found the temple where future me got the artifact that brought you here. It’s deep in Georios’ territory and infested with corrupted titankin, but I managed to sneak past safely. Since you came from the future with it, Agy assumed that there’d be another one somewhere in this time and told me to retrieve it.”

Phainon studies her carefully. “Yet there was no artifact?”

Cipher nods. “I found a mural instead. It took me a while to decipher it, but it was a warning about its use. The artifact’s power only lasts for seven days after the initial switch. So whether you liked it or not, both of you will be thrown back to your original timelines once the seven days are up.”

It’s good news. Or it should’ve been, if not for Cipher’s grim face. “Then what’s the catch?”

“… beside the mural, there was a paragraph etched on the wall. It cautions the person who wishes to borrow its power to be fully prepared for the consequences the switch may bring, as seeing the future does not guarantee its fruition.”

“Because the past version may choose completely different choices based on what they might’ve learned from it,” Phainon continues, understanding. “Is that what you’re afraid of, Lady Cipher?”

Her eyes flash with determination as she steps closer, jaw clenched tight. “I have never heard Agy sound as hopeful as she had in that voice message she left for me. Last time I heard it… It was a thousand years ago, back when the Imperator was still alive. Everyone got their happy ending, didn’t they?” Phainon nods. “Then I want to make sure it stays that way.”

Phainon nods. He’d been worrying about the same thing the moment he’d realized his past self might've gained information he’d never had access to before. “So do I. What do you have in mind?”

Cipher visibly sags in relief, the flicking of her tail less agitated as she points at the tome in his hands. “That is a fake manual I’ve made with a fake spell inside. I'm going to sneak into the lower levels of Marmoreal Palace’s vault and plant it in there for Agy or the others to find.”

“A fake spell,” Phainon repeats, then a sly smile curls his lips. “A spell that would mention the loss of memory about the switch once performed?”

“The power of Trickery is vast,” Cipher says, chin tilted stubbornly. Phainon pretends not to notice Bartholos sneakily listening in from the shadows. “If everyone takes a lie for the truth, the world would reshape itself under its authority.”

“A solid plan,” Phainon praises, “but quite a few flaws. For example, what happens when both parties attempt the spell at the same time? The power of Trickery is indeed vast, but there are greater authorities out there.” The Administrator, for example. Phainon’s tome displacement could simply be an unnoticeable glitch in the simulation, but if Zagreus was involved, Lygus was bound to notice.

Phainon had kept an eye out for him while he was here, then felt relieved when Aglaea informed him that Lygus had retreated from society for a sabbatical, and requested that he only be disturbed once there was a major emergency.

He was probably lurking in a cave somewhere, perfecting that stupid allegory of his. Knowing what he knows now, that was Lygus’ code for maintenance, and he’d be out of the loop for a while. How fortunate for all of them.

Cipher falters. “What do you suggest?”

“I want you to add a few conditions to the spell. One, that it must be performed after five days of the switch, and two, a priestess versed in time magic.”

“We don’t have one of those,” Cipher tells him.

Phainon shrugs. “Yes, but my timeline does have one. It’s to ensure that only one party would be capable of doing the spell,” When Cipher remains hesitant, he continues. “We can still make sure that everyone believes the lie. Let me work on the heirs while you ‘leak’ the details of the spell to the rest of Amphoreus. That way, everyone would believe it, and the memory wipe would be in effect.”

Cipher perks up, seemingly liking the plan a lot more. “And by the time you’re gone, everyone would assume that the people from your time had successfully cast the spell once they see past you take your place. The magic of Trickery would be triggered by your appearance.”

“And with me, who is well aware of this entire plan, back safely in the future, the magic would uphold until the time comes to close the loop. I assume you know what I mean.”

“Oh,” Cipher gasps. “I’ll have to steal the artifact, keeping it with me until the right time comes to hand it to you, so you’d be sent back to the past.”

“You’d also have to avoid past me to minimize the risk of the lie breaking and make sure that the fake tome stays right where it is in the safe for Aglaea or the others to find twenty years in the future,” Phainon supplies, softening as he looks back at Cipher. “I know it’s a huge burden to bear.”

“Hah,” Cipher scoffs, waving his concern away with a cavalier hand. “Please, I’m a thousand years old. What’s twenty years compared to that?”

“Ah, I’d like to request one final thing.”

“What is it?”

“Would it be within Trickery’s power to plant a vague seed of possibility into the laws of this world?”

Cipher blinks, confused. “I guess I could try. What do you have in mind?”

“Whenever you have the time, please go visit the Grove. Look for the deepest spot you can find and whisper the words ‘Protocol Agape’ into the roots of the Great Tree.”

Cipher looks curious, but to her credit, she doesn’t probe. “Alright. You’re helping me out here, so it’s only fair to help you out.”

“Thank you, Lady Cipher,” he smiles, then glances back at Mydei’s abode. “I should head back in.”

Cipher grins teasingly. “Sure, go back to your little husband. While I~ have a vault to break into,” she snatches the tome from him, waving a hand over it as she adds the conditions Phainon had set. “Toodles~”

“It’s why I recognized Augustus,” Phainon tells Mydei after he and Cipher revealed their plan. “You might’ve remembered rescuing him from an attempted assassination, but it was simply what the lie supplied after my presence was scrubbed from everyone's minds. Some of the jewelry you thought you’d purchased yourself was actually a courting gift from me.”

“So you did have fun with past me,” Mydei says dryly, earning a knowing giggle from Cipher. Phainon glances at her warningly, and she mimes zipping her lips. He’d really rather that Mydei didn’t know that Cipher knew of their bedroom dynamics.

“Wait, if you’re telling me now, does that mean the lie has been broken?” Mydei frowns. “Isn’t that dangerous?”

“Nope~” Cipher says, shaking her head. “With your husband’s return, the loop should be safely closed. The magic should lie with my past self now, who is about to keep the secret safe for twenty years.”

“Does that mean we’ll have our memories of that time back?”

Cipher shrugs. “It should trickle in slowly over the next few days. So we’ll have to wait and see.”

“Are you so desperate to know what I did back in the past, Mydei?” Phainon teases, jutting his lip out. “Oh, ye of little faith.”

“Yes,” Mydei deadpans. “I want to know exactly what kind of depravity you’ve inflicted on me.”

Phainon chortles, pressing another kiss to his husband’s forehead as he loops an arm around his waist. He can’t wait to see the look on his face when Mydei realizes how exactly he’d come to love calling him ‘Daddy’ in bed.

Mydei’s eyes narrow in suspicion. “What’s so funny?”

“Nothing, baby.”

Cipher, who apparently hadn’t left yet, snaps her fingers. “Nice touch with the Protocol Agape, by the way. It’s crazy how it actually worked.”

Protocol Agape was the code that helped Phainon transition from data to a tangible existence during his face-off with Nanook. According to Madame Herta, who’d managed to save Amphoreus’ coding after Lygus had attempted to destroy it, the protocol was not a local file, but something planted by an ‘unknown’ source.

Phainon had taken a gamble and won.

It had been a losing battle to get the Aeon to gaze at him, but his desperation to utterly destroy Irontomb inside out had managed to attract THEM in the end. He got the power he needed to destroy the threat and finally fulfilled his duty as the Deliverer.

It’s quite tiresome though, because apparently being glanced at meant he was one of THEIR Lord Ravagers now, though he has no intention of answering THEIR call.

“It was quite the close call, though. During that fight with Irontomb. I thought everything was over after I got stabbed and bled through the giant wound on my stomach,” Cipher sighs. “Everything would’ve unraveled had I died.”

Mydei swallows, his face turning grim at the memory of Cipher nearly dying in Aglaea’s arms. He breaks away from Phainon’s hold to wrap her in a hug, which she delightedly returns. “You truly are our Unsung Hero, Cipher. Everyone should know more of your deeds.”

“Psh, I didn’t do it for the recognition, you know,” she dismisses, but her smile is wide as she says, “But I appreciate the sentiment.”

“Come to our restaurant,” Phainon says as he steps closer, placing a hand over her shoulder. It’s their first contact ever, and the touch surprises her as much as it surprises him. “We’ll treat you. For life.”

Cipher cheers. “Woohoo! Now that's the kind of recognition I could get behind,” she spins around, nimbly jumping over their fence as she goes to leave. Then she pauses, as if remembering something. “Ah, by the way, little lion, did you already use that fake womb tattoo you bought from me?”

Mydei stiffens, face flushing as Phainon shoots him an intrigued look. Huh, Mydei made no mention of purchasing a womb tattoo before his time displacement. “Why?”

Cipher shoots him a mischievous grin. “Ya might want to watch out for some symptoms in the upcoming months,” she snickers. “After all, they were made with Trickery, heightening the already present desire to breed. And if you used it on the night of the fertility rite… who knows what would happen? Bye!”

She disappears in a puff of smoke. Phainon glances at Mydei, who’s determinedly avoiding eye contact as he fidgets in place. Phainon snickers. “Well, someone had a lot of fun during the festival.”

Mydei sputters as Phainon lifts him into a bridal carry. He carries Mydei into their home, intending on devouring him once he gets them both in bed. “Don't worry, baby,” he coos. “Daddy’s about to show you what real fun is.”

Mydei moans, burying his burning face into Phainon’s neck.

─── ⋆⋅☼⋅⋆ ───

Phainom blinks, squinting against the bright light. His entire body hurts, like it’s been put through a wringer. There’s also the feeling like he’d lost something, and he blinks back tears though he can’t recall what it is.

He realizes he’s been lying on a kline when pink, green, and white swim into his vision, and two pairs of eyes look down at him, one beady and one concerned.

“Lord Phainon,” Hyacine says gently, “are you alright? Lord Mydei found you face down in one of the baths. It seems like you slipped and bumped your head.”

Mydei? Phainon sits up, inwardly groaning at the pain that lances through his head. “I… don’t…” remember.

His eyes land on Hyacine and Ica, who are hovering over him and trying to chew on his hair if not for Hyacine holding her back. Then his eyes drift to Aglaea, who’s standing a few feet away with Trinnon, both looking concerned.

He spots Castorice standing even further away, her back against the wall as she wrings her hands nervously. She visibly sighs in relief when she sees he’s awake, and Phainon returns her smile as his eyes dart around until he finally finds the inconspicuous body of the one he’s been looking for.

“Looking a bit peaky there, Deliverer,” Mydei mocks, stepping closer once he notices Phainon’s attention on him. He crosses his arms, lips pursed into a frown (a pout) as he says, “To think I came all the way here after your invitation to bathe, yet I find you in a pool half-drowned.”

Did he really invite Mydei and succeed in actually getting him to come? Phainon can’t really remember. But he does stare up at Mydei stupidly, taking in his features that make his heart ache for some reason he can’t explain.

“I love you,” he blurts.

Hyacine immediately stands and walks away. Aglaea's brows raise and Trinnon gasps. Castorice makes a strangled noise and tries to muffle it by slapping her hand over her mouth. Mydei gapes at him, face flushing a pretty red and looking so, so beautiful.

Phainon smiles at him, calm as a breeze. Internally he panics, and he wants to smack himself. Oh Titans, why did he do that? He had a whole elaborate plan to court him, shower him with gifts, and his big mouth had to go and ruin it all.

“Deliverer, you…” Mydei’s voice cracks, trailing off. He turns to Hyacine, who’s stubbornly looking away from the mess. “Healer of Light, something’s clearly not right with him. We must move him to the Courtyard!”

“He’s fine,” Hyacine says flatly. She was one of the people who had the (mis)fortune of hearing and reading how Phainon waxed poetic about Mydei, so there was sadly nothing new about the declaration. “No concussion, not even a bump on the head.”

Mydei swallows, turning back to Phainon nervously. “I see.”

Thankfully, Aglaea wraps up the circus before anyone can spontaneously combust. Once she confirms that Phainon was completely fine, she dismisses the group and specifically sends Phainon home to rest. Phainon tries to protest, but immediately shuts up when she glares at him.

He’s at the main entrance of Marmoreal Palace, contemplating banging his head on the stairwell and scandalizing the citizens of Okhema for his display of absolute stupidity when someone clears their throat behind him. He turns, annoyed, then nearly jumps when he finds Mydei standing a few feet away.

“Deliverer… I,” Mydei shifts, looking hesitant for the first time since Phainon met him. He crosses his arms and looks away, incredibly shy. “Once you’re feeling better, you should come by the Kremnoan Settlement. We can have a spar since our plans have been derailed this time.”

Phainon stares at him, processing the words, then perks up as he bounds over excitedly. “Of course! I’ll be there first thing tomorrow!”

Mydei gives him an unimpressed look. “I said once you’re feeling better. Don’t push yourself unnecessarily and focus on your recovery.”

Phainon nods. “Mhm, and I’ll be all better tomorrow.”

Mydei sighs and begins to descend the stairs. “I’ll come by and bring you soup. Maybe it’ll fix whatever’s wrong with you.”

“Hey!” Phainon yelps as he follows, laughing as he takes in Mydei’s profile. An earring with a blue jewel glints under Kephale’s light. Hm, that was new. Did Mydei purchase it recently? “Nothing’s wrong with me.”

Mydei might not have acknowledged his confession exactly, but judging by his still-red ears and his willingness to hang around Phainon, he knows he has a chance.

And that was all he needed.
